text:
alex: Morning handoff — quick summary of the overnight page: autoscaler thrash on embeddings-prod pool caused transient 503/504s for a small set of Dedicated customers in us-central1. Pager started ~02:17; we contained it and are handing off the remaining follow-ups.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE fired (P1) embeddings-prod-usc autoscaler-flapping — 02:17 UTC. Linked ops runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-thrash

priya: Timeline: spike started ~01:55 UTC after a churn of many small embedding requests from partner X (batched client retries). Autoscaler attempted 3 scale-ups in 90s, instance provisioning queued, then backpressure hit the LB -> 503s. We saw increased GPU queue time + failed healthchecks.

dan: Immediate mitigations we applied: pinned model-embed-2 to existing nodes to avoid new model pulls, set temporary per-customer rate-limits (partner X) to throttle burst, bumped min-replicas from 2->4 for the pool, and turned on sticky routing to keep KV cache hot. That reduced 503s within ~12m.

sasha: Current state: autoscaler has stopped oscillating, pool healthy, tokenized p95 embeddings latency back to baseline (~120ms). Affected customers (3 Dedicated orgs) are seeing normal traffic now; one reported brief failures for ~10m.

mei: Evidence snippets from logs (truncated):
```
E 02:02:13 embedding-queue: enqueue latency spike 450ms
W 02:03:04 autoscaler: scale_up requested=4 current=1 reason=cpu+queue
E 02:03:46 healthcheck: instance init timeout 120s -> marking unhealthy
E 02:05:01 lb: upstream 503 x65
```

priya: Runbook refs used: autoscaler troubleshooting steps (section 2), dedicated fallback routing (section 4). Quick commands I ran: `kubectl patch hpa embeddings-prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":4}]'` and `redwoodctl routes set embeddings-prod --sticky true`.

ops-bot: Note: we also blocked a noisy API key temporarily via `rate-limit` for partner X (rule id rl-2026-0318-1).

alex: Who's next on shift? primary: priya (overnight responder), secondary: dan. Coverage gaps: no on-call in eu-west1 overnight for embedding failover (we have no cross-region auto-failover for Dedicated embeddings — licensing + model sync constraints). Need follow-up to define mitigation strategy for cross-region Dedicated customers.

dan: Action items for next 24h (handed to priya/dan/sasha):
- Postmortem owner: sasha (start draft, target 72h)
- Engineering follow-up: tune autoscaler debounce & stabilizer (owner: dan)
- Product/security: formalize per-customer burst protection (owner: priya)
- Ops: add synthetic canary that simulates small-batch embedding spikes (owner: mei)

priya: Customer comms: I'll draft incident note to the three affected Dedicated contacts, include timeline + mitigation + ETA for fixes. Want approvals from alex and sasha before sending.

sasha: Proposed longer-term fixes to discuss in postmortem: PID-style autoscaler dampening, grace-period for instance healthchecks during model pull, and model-pull prewarming for Dedicated pools. Also consider soft-fallback routing to hosted inference for low-risk customers.

alex: Next steps for on-call: keep monitoring autoscaler metrics (grafana: infra/embeddings/autoscaler), keep the partner X key throttled until we have a rate-limit rule in product, and reconvene async on the postmortem draft. If anything degrades again -> page the same channel and escalate to on-call rotation lead.

priya: Handing off — logs + commands + links pinned in #eng-oncall thread. I'll be online for the next 90 minutes then pass to dan at 10:00 UTC. :raised_hands:

dan: Acknowledged. I'll pick up monitoring and start the autoscaler tuning ticket.

oncall-bot: Handoff note recorded: primary=priya, secondary=dan, incident=autoscaler-thrash-2312345678, severity=P1.

alex: Thanks all. I'll sync w/ support for any customer escalation needs. If no regressions by EOD, normalizing to postmortem+retro cycle.
